The dorsal pattern most closely resembles that of clemsonar-phase jordani, but with some tendency toward glutinosus spatting. While variation occurs in the intensity of fleeking and spotting, all 23 specimens were basically similar to one another.
Apparently at Moody Spring the Plethodou population forms a slagle gene pool. The salamanders constituting this population are similar to glutinosus, but show some jordani influence. It is proposed that this population has arisen through introgression between glutinosus and jordani. As noted earlier, glutinosus is generally scarce on the escarpment, while Moody Spring is near the edge of the
contiguous range of fordani. Thus this population may represent another case of introgression on the periphery of a species range, where density of one or both perental species is low (Mayr, 1963).
At Burrells Mountain, less than two nules to the northeast of Moodly Spring, autinosis and fordani are distinct. Photographs of Plethodon from the two localities are given in Figure 2.
While more evidence is needed to establish this hypothesis, some areas along the southern edge of the Blue Ridge may present the necessary conditions for introgression between glatinosus and jurdani.
